# Testcases - risk-based acceptance specifications

383 cases generated from the SRS v0.1 blueprint: 370 offline, 13 live (26 e2e, 101 governance, 94 integration, 162 unit). Every entry is a written acceptance specification for a future system under test - not an executable test, not a mock echo and not a source-code inspection.

## Honest status

- **There is no application runtime in this repository.** Nothing has been executed and the default recorded status is `NOT_RUN`.
- This generator never records `PASS`. A successful generation run proves document integrity, reference validity and coverage bookkeeping - never system behaviour.
- Status vocabulary: `NOT_RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `SKIP_ASM_001`, `SKIP_UNIMPLEMENTED`, `BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE`.
- `SKIP_ASM_001` when the approved connector lock is absent, `SKIP_UNIMPLEMENTED` when the runtime is missing, `BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE` when a sandbox feature or policy lock is unavailable. A missing prerequisite is never `PASS`.

## What coverage does and does not mean

- Coverage here means **traceability**: every case names exact requirement tokens and coverage facets, and the generator refuses to write output when a mandatory facet token, a baseline case ID or an offline/live E2E counterpart is missing.
- Matching is exact-token set membership, never substring matching, so no ID can silently stand in for another.
- This is **not** an exhaustive claim over the whole checklist surface. Failure and boundary probes live in the unit and integration layers; E2E is limited to critical journeys.
- Baseline preservation: 218/218 current case IDs are retained exactly once, with mixed-case and dotted IDs preserved verbatim. An older draft mentioned 343 IDs; that set is not recoverable or verifiable here and is therefore not claimed.

## Strategy

```text
        E2E (e2e/offline.md + e2e/live.md)   few, critical complete journeys
     Integration (API, C360, FSM, command center, routing)
  Unit (skills, authority, business rules, knowledge, entities)
```

- Many fast isolated cases carry the failure, boundary and negative load; E2E carries complete outcomes with evidence.
- Every E2E case is paired offline/live with an identical requirement set, so the same observable contract is specified twice: against intercepted fixtures and against an approved sandbox.
- Cases are independent: each owns its namespace (`run_id` / `case_id` / `worker`), its setup and its cleanup. Waits are condition or deadline based, never fixed sleeps.
- Core policy, routing and evidence paths are never replaced by stubbed results.

## Offline vs live

| | Offline | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Data | [`fixtures/offline/`](fixtures/offline/) JSON system-of-record mocks | sandbox records created per case |
| Network | all vendor HTTP intercepted | approved sandbox endpoints only, never production |
| Identity | synthetic handles (`cust-a`, `SKU-OK`) | sandbox IDs mapped through gitignored `fixtures/live/env.local` |
| Evidence | mock/provider call logs | provider receipts plus audit records |
| Gate | none | approved ASM-001 connector lock, sandbox allowlist, approved recipients |
| Waiting | fixture/mock condition | provider webhook or status condition |
| Cleanup | reset namespaced mock state | retire only what the case created; keep immutable receipts |

## Regenerating

```bash
python testcases/_generate.py            # validate, then write docs, fixtures and manifest
python testcases/_generate.py --check    # validate and compare with disk; writes nothing
```

Python 3 standard library only, no network, no runtime: these case documents are specifications, and no runtime test was executed to produce them. Generation validates first and writes only after every check passes, each file through a temporary file plus an atomic replace, and it never rewrites `_generate.py`, `sources/*.py`, `sources/requirements.json` or `sources/baseline-ids.json`. Output is deterministic: regenerating without source changes leaves the tree byte-identical, and no timestamp or run state is embedded anywhere. `manifest.json` pins the SHA-256 of every input (SRS, inventory, baseline, source modules), and `--check` re-reads the generated files and the manifest and exits non-zero on validation errors, missing or stale output, and unexpected leftover generated files (for example an obsolete catalogue document). Errors are reported per case with the owning source module and position.

## Validation performed before any write

Required field types and detail minima (at least 3 named steps, 3 assertions, 2 forbidden results, 2 evidence items, 1 cleanup step, 2 preconditions, non-empty synthetic `inputs`, concrete `risk` and `automation` seam); unique case IDs with all baseline IDs retained exactly once; layer/suite agreement; valid environment, priority, gate and basis; reference paths that exist in the repository; requirement and facet tokens declared in `sources/requirements.json`; fixtures that exist in the merged source `FIXTURES`; complete mandatory facet coverage; every TC-E2E and PILOT criterion in both environments; symmetric offline/live E2E pairs with identical requirement sets and live prerequisites naming the approved ASM-001 lock.

Unclaimed requirement IDs are reported as coverage gaps in [`COVERAGE.md`](COVERAGE.md) and in `manifest.json`; unclaimed mandatory facet tokens are hard errors.

## Secrets, results and receipts

- [`fixtures/live/env.example`](fixtures/live/env.example) is a placeholder. Its presence is **not** approval: a live run still requires the approved ASM-001 lock and an allowlist.
- Real sandbox values belong in `fixtures/live/env.local` or the process environment, both kept out of git by [`.gitignore`](.gitignore). The generator never reads, writes or deletes local env files.
- Run results, receipts and scratch evidence stay in `results/`, which is gitignored. Sandbox receipts kept for audit are immutable: a case deletes only the records it created itself.
- Never mark a live case `PASS` without provider evidence, and never delete a sent message to pretend it was not sent.
